writeup: TIC 158398880 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.861461 days and a primary eclipse depth of 5.17 percent. The star does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel detection. Automated analysis of TESS photometry data produced a strong signal with a detection significance of 174.1. Pixel-level imaging analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 24.3, though the centroid offset of 5.4 arcseconds from the target position merits attention. No secondary eclipse was detected. One open question remains: the alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, which may indicate the true orbital period is twice what an initial analysis suggested; the corrected period of 6.861461 days accounts for this effect.
